title: $L^2$ error of the low-degree truncation
statement:
Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function, and for a natural number $k$ let $f_{\le k}(x) = \sum_{\abs{S}\le k} \hat f(S)\,\chi_S(x)$ be its low-degree part, retaining only the Fourier--Walsh coefficients of degree at most $k$. Then, under the uniform measure on the cube, the squared $L^2$ distance between $f$ and this truncation equals the total Fourier weight sitting above level $k$:
\[
  \E\big[(f(x) - f_{\le k}(x))^2\big] \;=\; \sum_{\abs{S} > k} \hat f(S)^2 .
\]
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean function of arity n
k is a natural number (the truncation level)
replaced:
The squared $L^2$ error of the degree-$k$ truncation is exactly the Fourier weight
above level $k$:
\[
  \E\big[(f - f_{\le k})^2\big] \;=\; \sum_{\abs{S} > k} \hat f(S)^2 .
\]
